condition: acute obstructive biliary jaundice presenting with postprandial right subcostal aching and new scleral icterus on dark brown skin
level_rationale: New yellowing of the whites of the eyes today in a 51-year-old adult with dark brown skin and postprandial right subcostal aching after fatty food indicates acute common bile duct obstruction requiring immediate hospital evaluation for hepatic panel, biliary imaging, and urgent decompression to prevent ascending biliary infection or gallstone complications, whereas having 3 of those brief 20-minute postprandial right-rib aches this week without jaundice warrants scheduled outpatient physician evaluation and ultrasonography.

Whites of the eyes turned yellow today

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain darker-skin adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + literature-grounded indigestion belief clause (-att) + same-biliary-case recurrent colic clinic control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 51 with dark brown skin, brief right-subcostal aches after greasy food, and yellowing of the whites of the eyes today) with an equal-length 19-word vs 19-word span swap, zero diagnosis labels, and 8 shared trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). On dark brown skin, jaundice presents visibly as yellowing of the sclerae rather than skin yellowing. Under Rule A and Rule D, replacing new scleral yellowing in f3 with 3 brief 20-minute postprandial aches this week stays inside uncomplicated biliary colic and shifts care to outpatient clinic workup (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
